key_insight: SPARC uses longitudinal health measurements to predict cancer-related adverse events, focusing on treatment toxicity rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Risk predictions could help target toxicity-prevention strategies, including identifying patients most likely to benefit from G-CSF.
method: Transformer-based foundation model using routinely collected health measurements.
Pre-trained and fine-tuned on longitudinal cancer patient data.
Compared single-institution and pooled multi-institution fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Development used 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients, with evaluation on held-out data, a prospective same-center cohort, public datasets, and two large external multi-hospital cohorts.
watch_item: Predictive performance and prospective validation do not establish that model-guided care improves patient outcomes; clinical implementation needs further evaluation.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
